To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the reported values of YM for any given tissue span several orders of magnitudes if the method of deformation (indentation versus tensile) is not considered; (2) when the method of deformation of a soft tissue is considered, then the reported values of the YM are consistently lower for indentation deformations compared to tensile deformations; (3) the difference between indentation and tensile measurements of YM is likely caused by the difference in the strain fields between the two methods; (4

the Young's modulus of soft biological tissues obtained from indentation deformations is lower than that obtained from tensile tests, and the difference between indentation and tensile tests can be as high as an order of magnitude.
the reported values of YM obtained from indentation and from tensile deformation of soft tissues are not the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an improved understanding of the biomechanical properties of soft tissues, and the role of these properties in disease and healing.
the mechanical behavior of soft biological tissues such as the brain, heart, lungs, and liver.
the development of an indentation technique for measuring YM of soft biological tissues in a manner that is comparable to tensile testing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

indentation and tensile measurements should be performed on the same tissue samples, or at least on samples from the same specimen, and that the method of deformation should be considered when comparing the results.
the reported YM values of soft biological tissues are dependent on both the tissue and the method of deformation.
, on average, the reported values of YM are consistently lower when measured by indentation deformations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
indentation is a better method than tension for obtaining the Young's modulus of soft biological tissues.
indentation and tensile tests are complementary methods that should be used in conjunction to obtain an accurate assessment of the material properties of biological tissues.
, for soft biological tissues, indentation is a more appropriate method for determining YM values.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the method of deformation should always be considered when interpreting the results from mechanical testing of soft tissues, and the method of deformation must be specified when reporting the results.

the reported YM values for soft biological tissues should always include the method of deformation used to measure YM, and this should be taken into consideration when comparing results across studies.
indentation is a less accurate and less precise method to determine the YM of soft biological tissues than tensile testing.
